verdict.rationale: Letta documents organization roles combined with sharing controls, and teammates' agents and conversations are private by default. This gives some role-based governance over who can access agents, which carry their memory. However, nothing shows memory-specific read/write policies or ACLs, and nothing shows audit logging of access; /doctor audits memory placement and duplication, not access. Missing for 10: memory-level read/write ACLs or policies, governance of which agents/tools can write memory, access audit logs, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can govern who and what can read or write memory with roles, policies, or access-control lists, and audit that access

citations.quote: Letta combines organization roles with sharing controls so teammates can collaborate without making all agent activity visible to the entire organization.
Membership lets teammates use the same organization while keeping each person's agents and conversations private by default.
You can share agents across your team (and set permissions for access) to create custom agents for your organization
